According to the document "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries" (ensm-2020), Table 1 is as follows:

| Process Technology or Cell Chemistry Modification | Areal Capacity Improvement (mAh/cm^2) | Calendered Electrode Thickness (μm) | Specific Capacity Improvement (mAh/g) | Estimated Energy Density Improvement (Wh/kg) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Section 4 – Water-Based Processing of | 6–8 | 110–150 | 160 | 225–250 |
| Cathodes (i.e. NMC 532) |  |  |  |  |
| Section 5 – Water-Based Processing of Si/C | 6.6–8.8 | 45–60 | 854 (15 wt% Si) | 250–275 |
| Anodes (N:P ¼ 1.1) |  |  |  |  |
| Section 6 – Low-Co/Ni-Rich Cathodes (i.e. | 6–8 | 90–125 | 190 | 275–300 |
| NMC 811) |  |  |  |  |
| Section 7 – Co-Free NFA | 4–6 | 65–100 | 180 | 250–275 |
| Section 8 – Coating Parameter and Drying | NA | 45–150 | NA | 220-240^a |
| Protocols |  |  |  |  |
| Section 9 – Ultra-High-Speed (Thick) | 8–8.8 | Anode – 110 | Anode – 854 | 325-350^b |
| Electrode Processing | Cathode – 260 | Cathode – 190 |  |  |
| (Uncalendered) |  |  |  |  |
| Section 10- Ultra-Fast Formation Cycling | NA | NA | 150^a | 260-280^a,b |

The technologies with the highest upper bound of estimated energy density improvement are:

* Section 9 – Ultra-High-Speed (Thick) Electrode Processing (325-350 Wh/kg)
* Section 10- Ultra-Fast Formation Cycling (260-280 Wh/kg)

The technology with the lowest upper bound of estimated energy density improvement is:

* Section 7 – Co-Free NFA (250-275 Wh/kg)

The upper bounds of estimated energy density improvement for these technologies are 55-70 Wh/kg apart.

prompt.system: You answer questions using only the documents below: pages selected from them, with tables written row by row. Answer briefly. If you compute a number, show the calculation. If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so.

expect: highest: Section 9 ultra-high-speed (thick) electrode processing, 325-350 Wh/kg; lowest: Section 8 coating parameter and drying protocols, 220-240; 350 - 240 = 110 Wh/kg
question: In Table 1, which technologies have the highest and the lowest upper bound of estimated energy density improvement, and how far apart are those bounds?
